items.title: Send these readings to your care team today
items.text: Your blood sugar readings were higher than the target, so contact your care team today to discuss what you can do. Your average reading was 235.2 mg/dL, which is higher than the usual target of under 5% above 250 mg/dL.

items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: In real adults (CGMacros), a walk after a meal went with a rise only about 3.2 mg/dL smaller (95% CI -6.9 to 0.5): not distinguishable from zero. You walked after 2 of your scored meals, too few to measure your own effect yet. In the synthetic program, a walk after dinner went with a rise about 18.3 mg/dL smaller in the same person, more than after other meals (14.6 mg/dL). 10 to 19 minutes got most of the gain: 17.5 mg/dL less, against 19.5 for 20-29 minutes and 16.6 for 30+ minutes.

rejected.text: Walking after a meal may help with blood sugar, as it went with a rise about 3.2 mg/dL smaller in some adults. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes, like 17.5 mg/dL less, may be enough to get most of the gain.

items.title: Move dinner earlier
items.text: Eating dinner late, like you did 100.0% of the time, went with sugar rising about 9.2 mg/dL more than earlier dinners. Try to start dinner before 8 pm, as sugar rose about 13.3 mg/dL more after a dinner at 8-9 pm than before 6 pm.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: Your overnight fast averaged 9.8 hours, which is less than some other periods, like 13 hours. Adding an overnight fast to coaching changed some numbers by -0.03 points compared with coaching alone, but this is still being studied.
